name: Naloxone

summary: Opioid antagonist for complete or partial reversal of opioid depression, including respiratory depression. Nursing focus: precipitated withdrawal in opioid-dependent patients, continued observation and the effects reported after use.

jurisdiction_note: US FDA label only. EMA, MHRA and SFDA labels were not read; indications, warnings and presentations differ by country and by manufacturer.

items.text: The label indicates naloxone hydrochloride injection for the complete or partial reversal of opioid depression, including respiratory depression, induced by natural and synthetic opioids.
Keep the patient under close observation after reversal, and report the return of sedation or slow breathing.
Monitoring frequency and alarm limits follow the unit's protocol for this medicine.

The label calls for keeping a patient who has responded to naloxone under continued surveillance, since the duration of action of some opioids may exceed that of naloxone; it also notes naloxone is not effective against respiratory depression from non-opioid drugs, and that reversal by partial agonists may be incomplete, in which case breathing should be mechanically assisted as clinically indicated.
Naloxone should be given cautiously to people known or suspected to be physically dependent on opioids, because abrupt and complete reversal may precipitate an acute withdrawal syndrome.

Withdrawal signs may include body aches, diarrhoea, tachycardia, fever, runny nose, sneezing, sweating, yawning, nausea or vomiting, restlessness, shivering and increased blood pressure; neonates may also show convulsions.
In postoperative patients the label lists hypotension, hypertension and ventricular tachycardia and fibrillation among the associated adverse events.
Call for help for recurring sedation or slow breathing, a new arrhythmia, marked blood pressure changes or withdrawal signs.
Record the product and order checks, monitoring results, adverse events and escalation per unit standard.
Institution-specific preparation: follow your pharmacy's preparation standard and the product labelling. This library gives no preparation or concentration instructions.
Institution-specific dosing: follow the prescriber's order and your institution's approved protocol. This library gives no dosing instructions.

monitoring.text: Watch breathing and level of consciousness closely after reversal.
Note opioid dependence and watch for withdrawal signs.
Call for help if sedation or slow breathing returns.
Record the event, the response and observations.
